bull.b: Broad OEM coverage and Hyster-Yale certification can strengthen Flux Power’s access to established industrial-vehicle channels. These relationships may improve customer credibility, expand qualification opportunities, and support more durable adoption of its lithium-ion systems as fleets electrify.

SkyEMS 3.0 adds monitoring and AI capabilities to the battery offering, helping differentiate Flux Power beyond hardware alone. Broad inclusion across GFC batteries can deepen customer integration, support fleet uptime, and create a stronger platform for repeat product adoption.

The materially lower expense base improves the company’s ability to control losses while revenue recovers. If demand normalizes, retaining these efficiencies could provide operating leverage and reduce the sales level needed to move toward sustainable profitability.

bear.b: Dependence on a significant customer makes revenue vulnerable to that account’s capital-allocation decisions. The resulting sales disruption can reduce production scale, weaken operating leverage, and make recovery less predictable even as other OEM and channel initiatives progress.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is not currently funding operations internally. Continued losses and cash consumption can restrict investment in growth, increase reliance on financing, and make execution more sensitive to revenue volatility.

A thin equity cushion and lender default status materially reduce financial flexibility. The required equity raise may create dilution or funding pressure, while tighter reporting and lender discretion can constrain capital allocation and heighten the risk around ongoing operations.
